name: V4: ramjet lights in the dive at M 0.50; modelled pitch arcs; spiral climb
how_to_refly: SIMPLE_MODEL_CD0_FRONTAL=0.1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/Scripts/python scripts/fly_frozen_v4.py   -- locked by tests/test_v4_frozen.py, which runs it in a SUBPROCESS because CD0 is baked at import time (docs/v3_learnings_for_v4.md 5.2 #19).

geometry_change_from_v3b.what: the chamber diameter BECOMES the body diameter: 225.2 -> 214.0 mm
geometry_change_from_v3b.why: user directive 2026-08-13 -- delete the 5.6 mm annular gap that never fit the side valve runners anyway (learnings 5.2 #16)
geometry_change_from_v3b.consequence_1: simple_model has ONE diameter (pulsejet_simple builds chamber volume from diameter_m), so the chamber shrinks 9.7% along with the frontal area. This model does NOT claim the free drag reduction a split body/chamber would give. medium_model keeping a true 214 mm chamber inside a 214 mm skin will measure MORE thrust than this -- the safe direction.
geometry_change_from_v3b.consequence_2: V3b's 121.6 mm throat against a 214 mm body is area fraction 0.323, over PULSEJET_MAX_THROAT_AREA_FRACTION = 0.30, which zeroes the engine outright. The throat is held at V3b's OWN area fraction (0.29160) instead, forcing 121.6 -> 115.6 mm.

gates.ramjet_lights_in_the_dive: PASS -- M 0.500 at 503.5 m, inside v3_dive (the V4 requirement)
gates.400ft_floor_held: PASS (flown minimum 149.23 m vs 121.92 m floor -- the arc bottoms out above it)
gates.safe_landing: PASS -- only because the climb is a SPIRAL; a straight climb to the same top cuts off 17.5 km downrange and lands 4-6 km short of home
gates.min_traverse_accel_0.25g: FAIL (0.163) -- the cost of a 0.50 gate; 0.42 gate gives 0.415 g on the same airframe
gates.min_powered_accel_positive: FAIL (-0.021 g at the top of climb) -- the vehicle is AT its climb ceiling at 1100 m; negative at every top >= 800 m
gates.min_powered_thrust_margin_1.15: FAIL (0.855) -- engine-only margin at lightoff; never met by any V2/V3/V4 configuration

known_risks: Top of climb 1100 m sits just under the FP pulsejet flame-out ceiling (~1250 m alive / 1275 m dead at CONFIRM, and that ceiling DROPPED ~200 m when the grid was refined 162 -> 324). This is the single largest cross-model risk in the design.

min_powered_accel_g is -0.021 g at the top of climb: the vehicle is asymptotically at its climb ceiling, not stalling, but there is no margin there. simple_model has no flame-out model at all -- it only lapses thrust as (rho/rho_SL)^3.
The M 0.50 gate survives a 10% pulsejet thrust cut in this model. Closed-form runs 6-16% high on thrust vs FP, so 10% is coverage, not comfort.

Reachability was screened closed-form, which docs/v3_learnings_for_v4.md 4.1 says is exactly the wrong tool for a 'can it reach X' question. The -10% haircut is the mitigation, not a substitute for an FP check.
The spiral climb charges bank load (n = cos(gamma)/cos(30 deg) = 1.155) and therefore induced drag, but does NOT model roll-in/roll-out or heading alignment before the pushover.
Side valve runners still do not fit inside a 214 mm skin -- an external fairing is needed and its drag is not in this CD0.

alternative_more_payload_less_robust.trajectory: top 1100 m, dive 18 deg, climb 8 deg spiral, pull-out 2.0 g nominal, same gate 0.50
alternative_more_payload_less_robust.why_not_chosen: better on all four of the user's stated criteria (payload, T/W, body load, and traverse) but tolerates 8% thrust loss instead of 10%. V3's headline failure (V3c) was a design that passed at one fidelity and failed outright at the next, so robustness was taken as the tiebreak. Switching is a one-line change in out_simple_model/v4_pick.json.
